properties.name: Bivalence: every proposition is exactly one of true or false
properties.statement: Every proposition takes exactly one of two truth values, true or false. This is the classical semantics the truth tables rest on; it is taken as given here, not argued for.

properties.name: Definition: the truth tables of not, and, or, and what equivalence means
properties.statement: ¬P is true exactly when P is false; P∧Q is true exactly when both are true; P∨Q is true exactly when at least one is true. P ≡ Q (semantic equivalence) means P and Q take the same value under every assignment of truth values to their variables.

properties.name: Definition: NAND, P↑Q := ¬(P∧Q)
properties.statement: P↑Q (NAND) is defined as ¬(P∧Q). In the natural-deduction proofs a formula written with ↑ is read as its unfolded form; a step that relies on the unfolding lists this definition as a premise.

properties.name: Rule ∧E (and-elimination)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P∧Q, infer P; from P∧Q, infer Q.

properties.name: Rule ∧I (and-introduction)
properties.source: Natural deduction in Gentzen's style (G. Gentzen, 'Untersuchungen über das logische Schließen', Mathematische Zeitschrift 39, 1935; D. Prawitz, Natural Deduction, 1965). RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P and Q, infer P∧Q.

properties.name: Rule ↔I (biconditional introduction)
properties.source: Standard; ↔ taken as (P→Q)∧(Q→P). RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P→Q and Q→P, infer P↔Q. In natural deduction P ≡ Q is proved as P↔Q.

properties.name: Rule →E (modus ponens)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P→Q and P, infer Q.

properties.name: Rule →I (conditional proof)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From a derivation of Q under the assumption P, infer P→Q, discharging P.

properties.name: Rule ¬E (contradiction: from P and ¬P, falsum)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction (¬P read as P→⊥). RECALLED, not read.

properties.name: Rule ¬I (negation introduction; intuitionistically valid)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From a derivation of ⊥ under the assumption P, infer ¬P, discharging P. Valid intuitionistically as well as classically.

properties.name: Rule ∨E (or-elimination, proof by cases)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P∨Q, a derivation of R under the assumption P, and a derivation of R under the assumption Q, infer R, discharging both assumptions. The disjunction P∨Q is what makes the two cases exhaustive.

properties.name: Rule ∨I (or-introduction)
properties.source: Gentzen 1935 / Prawitz 1965 natural deduction. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: From P, infer P∨Q; from Q, infer P∨Q.

properties.name: Rule RAA (classical reductio ad absurdum) — the classical rule
properties.source: Prawitz, Natural Deduction (1965), classical rule ⊥c. RECALLED, not read; the interderivability remark is also recalled.
properties.statement: From a derivation of ⊥ under the assumption ¬P, infer P, discharging ¬P. This is the one classical rule in the system: without it the rules above are intuitionistic logic. Recalled: over the intuitionistic rules, RAA, double-negation elimination (¬¬P ⊢ P) and excluded middle (⊢ P∨¬P) are interderivable.

properties.name: Rule: uniform substitution into a derived schema
properties.source: Standard metatheorem of propositional logic, used here as a rule. RECALLED, not read.
properties.statement: A formula schema derived with every supposition discharged holds for any formula substituted uniformly for one of its letters (e.g. B for A).

properties.name: Logic rung: De Morgan, NAND, excluded middle (proof trial)
properties.objective: Each law is proven twice, by an exhaustive truth table and by natural deduction, and excluded middle shows an axiom as a choice.

properties.context_setter: The project's objective says excluded middle should show an axiom as a choice.
properties.question: Excluded middle's truth-table line rests on bivalence (every proposition is true or false), which is close to the law itself; its natural-deduction line rests on the classical rule RAA. Do you want both lines kept as proofs, or should the record say plainly that each line moves the law into a chosen foundation rather than deriving it from nothing?

properties.answer: "Accept + record gap": ∨E stands as the exhaustiveness record for these proofs; the gap (exhaustiveness cannot point at an assumed disjunction) will be recorded by the observer. (Relayed by the observer, 2026-10-19.)
properties.context_setter: Proof by cases is used in De Morgan (both forms) and in the OR-by-NAND part of law 2.
properties.question: In three proofs by cases (∨E), what makes the two cases all the cases is the disjunction being split, which is itself a supposition inside the proof. reflow2 judged that supposition by its own standing status and read the step 'unknown', so I named the rule ∨E (taken as given) as the exhaustiveness record instead. Do you accept the rule ∨E as that record?

properties.answer: "Identities + cited corollary": law 2 is the three identities; add the corollary that NAND is functionally complete, resting on them plus the cited theorem that {∧,∨,¬} is functionally complete (DNF), recalled (Sheffer 1913; Peirce 1880 unpublished). (Relayed by the observer, 2026-10-19.)
properties.context_setter: Law 2 is recorded with a truth table over 4 rows and a natural-deduction proof of the three identities.
properties.question: Law 2 says NAND alone can express NOT, AND and OR. I proved exactly the three identities ¬A ≡ A↑A, A∧B ≡ (A↑B)↑(A↑B), A∨B ≡ (A↑A)↑(B↑B). Is that the claim you mean, or do you also want functional completeness (every truth function of any number of variables is expressible with NAND alone), which needs a further argument by induction on formulas?

properties.statement: Every truth function of n variables is expressed by a formula using only ∧, ∨ and ¬: its disjunctive normal form, one conjunction of literals per row where it is true (and A∧¬A if none).

properties.name: Cited: classical propositional natural deduction is sound and complete
properties.source: RECALLED, not read: completeness of the propositional calculus, E. Post, 'Introduction to a general theory of elementary propositions', American Journal of Mathematics 43 (1921); for natural deduction, D. Prawitz, Natural Deduction (1965). Recorded on the owner's word (2026-10-19, relayed by the observer): 'Both, linked by citation'.
properties.statement: For propositional formulas: ⊢ P (derivable in classical natural deduction) if and only if ⊨ P (true under every assignment). Soundness: derivable implies valid; completeness: valid implies derivable. Used to read each law's two lines as establishing one ≡.

properties.name: Law 1: De Morgan's laws, both
properties.statement: For all propositions A and B: ¬(A∧B) ≡ ¬A∨¬B, and ¬(A∨B) ≡ ¬A∧¬B.

properties.name: ⊥ by cases on ¬A∨¬B
properties.statement: Contradiction, in either case of ¬A∨¬B, under A∧B.

properties.name: Suppose ¬(A∧B)
properties.statement: Hypothesis for →I (De Morgan, ∧ form, forward direction): ¬(A∧B).

properties.name: A∧B (from A, B)
properties.statement: A∧B, under the suppositions A and B.

properties.name: ¬A∨¬B (from ¬B)
properties.statement: ¬A∨¬B, from ¬B by ∨I (one occurrence of the formula, under ¬(A∧B) and A).

properties.name: ¬A∨¬B (from ¬A)
properties.statement: ¬A∨¬B, from ¬A by ∨I (a second occurrence of the formula, under ¬(A∧B) and ¬(¬A∨¬B)).

properties.name: Case A
properties.statement: Case hypothesis (first disjunct of A∨B): A.

properties.name: Case B
properties.statement: Case hypothesis (second disjunct of A∨B): B.

properties.name: ⊥ in case A
properties.statement: Contradiction in case A: A and ¬A.

properties.name: ⊥ in case B
properties.statement: Contradiction in case B: B and ¬B.

properties.name: ⊥ by cases on A∨B
properties.statement: Contradiction in either case of A∨B, under ¬A∧¬B.

properties.name: ¬(A∨B) ↔ ¬A∧¬B (natural deduction)
properties.statement: ⊢ ¬(A∨B) ↔ ¬A∧¬B, derived in natural deduction without the classical rule.

properties.name: Suppose A (to refute it, excluded middle)
Suppose ¬(A∧B), i.e. A↑B, for reductio
properties.statement: Hypothesis for classical reductio: ¬(A∧B), which is A↑B.

properties.name: A∧B ↔ (A↑B)↑(A↑B) (natural deduction)
properties.statement: ⊢ A∧B ↔ (A↑B)↑(A↑B): AND is expressed by NAND.

properties.name: Law 2: NAND alone can express NOT, AND and OR
properties.statement: For all propositions A and B: ¬A ≡ A↑A; A∧B ≡ (A↑B)↑(A↑B); A∨B ≡ (A↑A)↑(B↑B), where P↑Q := ¬(P∧Q).

properties.name: Corollary: NAND is functionally complete
properties.statement: Every truth function of any number of variables is expressible using ↑ (NAND) alone.

properties.name: Suppose A (to refute it, NOT by NAND)
¬A ↔ A↑A (natural deduction)
properties.statement: ⊢ ¬A ↔ A↑A: NOT is expressed by NAND.

properties.name: A↑A, i.e. ¬(A∧A) (under ¬A)
properties.statement: ¬(A∧A), which is A↑A by definition, under ¬A.

properties.name: Case A (OR by NAND)
properties.statement: Case hypothesis (first disjunct of A∨B): A.

properties.name: Case B (OR by NAND)
properties.statement: Case hypothesis (second disjunct of A∨B): B.

properties.name: ⊥ in case A (OR by NAND)
properties.statement: Contradiction in case A: A∧A and ¬(A∧A).

properties.name: ⊥ in case B (OR by NAND)
properties.statement: Contradiction in case B: B∧B and ¬(B∧B).

properties.name: ⊥ by cases on A∨B (OR by NAND)
properties.statement: Contradiction in either case of A∨B, under (A↑A)∧(B↑B).

properties.name: A∨B ↔ (A↑A)↑(B↑B) (natural deduction)
properties.statement: ⊢ A∨B ↔ (A↑A)↑(B↑B): OR is expressed by NAND.

properties.name: ¬B → B↑B (the NOT lemma with B for A)
properties.statement: ¬B → B↑B, by substituting B for A in the lemma ¬A → A↑A.

properties.name: A↑A (from ¬A, by the NOT lemma)
properties.statement: A↑A, from ¬A and the lemma ¬A → A↑A by →E.
